standard.title: Sounds, pronunciation and intonation patterns
standard.description: recognise and use modelled combinations of sounds, pronunciation and intonation patterns of the target language to form words and phrases
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise and imitate target language sounds and basic intonation patterns (AC9LS2U01). They imitate challenging sounds and distinguish statement and question intonation. They have not yet applied sound knowledge systematically to spell new words or encountered accent marking functions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise and use modelled sound combinations, pronunciation patterns and intonation in the target language — applying sound-to-spelling knowledge and distinguishing intonation across a range of sentence types.

nodes.label: Sound patterns, spelling and consonant conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use knowledge of target language sound patterns to predict spellings of new words and recognise consonant conventions in familiar vocabulary.
nodes.minimum_width: Use sound knowledge to predict the spelling of at least two unfamiliar words based on known patterns; identify at least one consonant convention in context.
nodes.typical_width: Apply sound-to-spelling knowledge to predict new word spellings; apply known consonant conventions; apply accent marks correctly in familiar words; use vocabulary pattern knowledge to extend pronunciation to unfamiliar words; play sound-based games.
wider: Apply a spelling pattern to a set of unfamiliar words — check predictions against a reference and identify which patterns were most reliable
Explain a target language spelling or pronunciation rule using examples — demonstrating metalinguistic understanding
nodes.hinge_reason: Sound-to-spelling prediction is the mechanism that allows students to extend written vocabulary beyond memorised words. Students who cannot apply sound patterns to new words are dependent on rote memorisation — severely limiting written vocabulary growth.

response_modes.reason: Spelling prediction from sound patterns requires explicit rule awareness — students need to articulate the pattern before they can apply it to new words.

success_criteria: Predicts the spelling of at least two unfamiliar words using known sound patterns with adequate accuracy
Identifies at least one consonant convention in a familiar word and produces it correctly

nodes.label: Intonation across sentence types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and use different intonation patterns across statement, question, command and exclamation sentence types.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least three different sentence types with correct intonation; demonstrate intonation variation in spoken production.
nodes.typical_width: Use correct intonation for statements, questions, commands and exclamations; apply varied pace, stress and rhythm in spoken performance; understand how pitch and stress modify meaning; apply prosodic features in songs, chants and oral activities.
wider: Demonstrate how changing only intonation changes the meaning of the same sentence — produce at least three intonation variants and explain the communicative difference
Perform a familiar chant or spoken text with deliberate prosodic control — demonstrating attention to rhythm, stress and pace beyond word-level accuracy

response_modes.reason: Intonation control across sentence types develops through performance across varied communicative contexts. Each context demands different intonation conditions; varied performance builds prosodic range.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Intonation awareness — understanding that the same words mean different things with different intonation — is a metalinguistic insight with genuine communicative value.
success_criteria: Produces three distinct sentence types with correct intonation patterns
Demonstrates different intonation for at least one statement-question pair
